clue.text: Come back to gather fruit

parts.note: to reap is to gather in a harvest
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: Someone returns to the orchard to pick the crop.
explanation.definitionFit: To return after an absence is to be seen again, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Shrink is about to medicate

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to treat is to medicate

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist is going to prescribe drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrink' looks like slang for a psychiatrist; it is the verb, to draw back.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrink back or recoil is to withdraw, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: First off, just look

indicators.note: first off says the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: fair means just

explanation.surface: An instruction: before anything else, simply look.
explanation.definitionFit: An appearance or manner, as in an air of confidence, is a look.

clue.text: Highly valued clothing company is strikingly advanced

indicators.note: clothing means the valued word dresses round the other

parts.note: precious means highly valued

explanation.surface: A prized fashion firm is boldly ahead of its time.
explanation.definitionFit: A child developed far beyond its years is remarkably forward for its age.

clue.text: Caucasian needs capital, possessing almost nothing

indicators.note: possessing means the capital letters hold the shortened nothing

parts.note: A1 means capital or first-rate, written AI with I for one

indicators.note: almost means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: zero is nothing

explanation.surface: A white person needs money but has hardly any.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caucasian' suggests a white person, but means from the Caucasus. 'Capital' reads as money; it is A1, first-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Azerbaijan is in the Caucasus region, so its people are Caucasian in the geographical sense.

clue.text: Case involving European institute

indicators.note: involving means the case wraps round the other letter

parts.note: a crate is a packing case

explanation.surface: A legal case concerning some European body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' and 'institute' read as legal and academic nouns; 'institute' is in fact the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To institute something is to set it up or found it, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Perhaps bay tree lacks width

indicators.note: lacks means the tree goes without that letter

parts.note: the rowan is a tree, the mountain ash

explanation.surface: A bay tree that is rather narrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bay tree' reads as the laurel; 'bay' is a horse's colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Bay is a reddish-brown horse colour, and this word is another horse colouring, so bay is an example.

clue.text: A day before a party, providing booze

parts.note: Mon is short for Monday
till means until, before
a do is a party

explanation.surface: One day ahead of a party, there's drink laid on.
explanation.definitionFit: A medium-dry sherry from Spain, so an example of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: E-books doubled English understanding

indicators.note: doubled means the electronic-books pair appears twice

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Digital books twice over helped someone grasp the language.
explanation.definitionFit: An agreement between nations, as in the Entente Cordiale, is an understanding.

clue.text: Island city capital with mounting deprivation

parts.note: Lima is the capital of Peru

indicators.note: mounting in a down clue means the word reads upwards

parts.note: loss is deprivation

explanation.surface: A capital city where poverty is rising.
explanation.definitionFit: A port city on the island of Cyprus, so the definition is a fair description.

clue.text: Book title that's a cryptic hint to get agent male fellowship?

wordplay.reading: GENT MALE FELLOW in A SHIP

parts.note: the words picture GENT, MALE and FELLOW, three words for a man, sitting between A and SHIP, so inside 'a ship', which is a boat

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a novel whose title hints at a fraternity of men.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the title as an instruction: put three men (GENT, MALE, FELLOW) in A ... SHIP (a boat) and you get A-GENT MALE FELLOW-SHIP, the clue's last three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerome K. Jerome's comic 1889 novel about a rowing holiday on the Thames bears this name.

clue.text: Green energy, reason to cut fossil fuel

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: to cut means the reasoning word slices into the fuel

parts.note: coal is a fossil fuel
logic is reasoning

explanation.surface: An environmental argument: renewable energy is a reason to reduce coal burning.
explanation.definitionFit: Green in the political sense means environmentally friendly, concerned with nature.

clue.text: Stubborn offender's first confined to house arrest after vacation

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of offender's
to house means the bound word contains the next piece

parts.note: pinioned means held with the arms bound

indicators.note: after vacation means arrest is emptied, leaving only its ends

explanation.surface: A stubborn criminal was first held under house arrest after being evicted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after vacation' means arrest is emptied of its middle letters. 'house arrest' reads as one phrase, but 'house' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone obstinately sure of their own views is dogmatic, so stubborn fits.

clue.text: Briefly check for shock

indicators.note: briefly says the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: to stunt growth is to check it

explanation.surface: A quick check to see whether someone is in shock.
explanation.definitionFit: To shock someone is to daze or stagger them, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Even Sherpa finally is lost, with trail disappearing

indicators.note: is lost suggests the letters wander out of their order
finally picks the last letter of Sherpa

parts.note: a scent is a trail followed by hounds

explanation.surface: Even a mountain guide gets lost when the path vanishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is lost' rearranges EVEN plus A into EVANE.
explanation.definitionFit: Fading quickly from sight or memory, transient, is what vanishing means.

clue.text: Greasing the wheels after seat finally is occupied by Labour?

indicators.note: after puts the lubrication word behind the single letter
finally points to the last letter of seat

parts.note: oiling is greasing wheels, literally

explanation.surface: A political picture: smoothing the way once a parliamentary seat is won by the Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' is capitalised to suggest the UK political party; read it as plain hard work. The question mark flags that playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone working hard is busy at, or occupied by, labour in the sense of toil.

clue.text: Be gentle with, say, one shattered after game

indicators.note: after puts the scrambled letters behind the game

parts.note: Go is a Japanese board game

indicators.note: shattered means the words are broken and reassembled

explanation.surface: Take it easy on, say, a player worn out after a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shattered' looks like 'exhausted'; it rearranges SAY ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning to treat someone leniently, not harshly.

clue.text: Is around Le Figaro's locality

indicators.note: around means the word for being alive is turned back to front

parts.note: one who is alive lives, so is can stand for lives

explanation.surface: A question about where the French newspaper Le Figaro is based.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Le Figaro' looks like the French newspaper; 'Le' is just letters and Figaro is the barber of Rossini's opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Rossini's opera The Barber of Seville is set in that Spanish city, home of the barber Figaro.

clue.text: Attack decapitated blue whale first

indicators.note: first puts the whale ahead of the colour

parts.note: the sei is a species of rorqual whale

indicators.note: decapitated means the colour loses its first letter

parts.note: azure is sky blue

explanation.surface: A blue whale attacks, headfirst.
explanation.definitionFit: A fit or sudden attack of illness, as in an epileptic attack, is a medical sense.

clue.text: Influential group of students changing sides

indicators.note: changing sides means right, R, swaps to left, L

parts.note: a seminar is a small study group

explanation.surface: A powerful student society defects.
explanation.definitionFit: Highly original and shaping later developments, as in a groundbreaking paper.

clue.text: Injured a leg in the middle of steep descent

indicators.note: injured suggests the words are damaged and rearranged
the middle of picks the central letter of steep

explanation.surface: Someone hurt a leg halfway down a steep slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Injured' rearranges A LEG IN to LINEAG. 'Steep descent' looks like a slope, but 'descent' alone means ancestry.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancestry, a line of forebears, is what one's descent means in genealogy.

clue.text: One sent off to support recording artist

indicators.note: to support in a down clue puts these letters below the record

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: off suggests the letters are disordered

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A singer is dropped from a label to back a recording star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recording artist' reads as one phrase; the definition is 'artist' alone. 'off' rearranges I and SENT to STEIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Jacob, the American-born British sculptor, bore this surname.

clue.text: Doctor embraces home care

indicators.note: embraces means the doctor letters surround the other word

parts.note: MD is a Doctor of Medicine
in means at home

explanation.surface: A doctor who takes up care at home.
explanation.definitionFit: To look after something, as in minding the children, is to care for it.

clue.text: Being around one boring idiot leads to calumnies

indicators.note: boring means drilling into the fool word

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: around means the being wraps the numeral

parts.note: a being is a person
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Being near a tedious fool provokes slanderous remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' looks like 'dull', but means drilling into the fool; 'around' wraps the being round the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Slanders or defamatory remarks, which is what calumnies are, cast on someone's character.

clue.text: Recruit learning about Navy gets upset

indicators.note: gets upset in a down clue means the whole is turned upside down
about means the learning word goes round the letter

parts.note: lore is learning

explanation.surface: A trainee finds out about the Navy and is distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts N in LORE for LORNE; 'gets upset' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign someone up as a member or trainee is to enlist them, as a verb.

clue.text: Take part in initiation ceremony at any time

indicators.note: Take part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An invitation to join in a rite of passage.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as in 'if once you start', meaning ever or whenever.

clue.text: Break lonely routine? No, never!

indicators.note: break suggests the words are smashed and the pieces rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to escape a solitary rut and firmly refuses.
explanation.walkthrough: This is British slang for 'certainly not'; Nellie is rhyming slang (Nellie Duff, puff, breath of life).
explanation.definitionFit: An emphatic British refusal, equal to 'certainly not' or 'no way'.

clue.text: Press fabrication

parts.note: a story invented by the newspapers is a falsehood

explanation.surface: A made-up newspaper story.
explanation.definitionFit: An untruth is what any fabrication is, here one printed by journalists.

clue.text: Run summer league at first

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of league

parts.note: a summer here is one who sums, an adder

explanation.surface: Organising a summer sports league for the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summer' is not the season but someone who adds up.
explanation.definitionFit: A run in tights or stockings, a vertical strip of unravelled stitches, is also called this.

clue.text: Strict about toilet? She won't be!

definitions.text: Strict about toilet? She won't be!

indicators.note: about means the strict word goes round the toilet word

parts.note: stern means strict
lat is short for latrine, a toilet

explanation.surface: A remark about someone fussy over the bathroom, and a woman who is anything but.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirty, untidy woman, an old-fashioned term, would hardly be fussy about cleanliness.
